question.text:
CASE STUDY (continued): Mrs. Lakshmi redeemed Rs. 5 lakh from one of her equity schemes on Monday at 2 PM. It is now Friday (5 working days later) and she has not received the redemption proceeds in her bank account.
Question 4: What is the correct course of action for Mrs. Lakshmi regarding her delayed redemption proceeds?

answer.text: She should wait for 10 working days as that is the standard turnaround time for equity fund redemptions
She should redeem additional units to check if the payment system is working

She should complain to the AMC first, as the 3 working day deadline has been breached, and the AMC is liable to pay her interest at 15% per annum for the delay period; if unresolved, she can escalate to SEBI SCORES
She cannot complain as the delay is within the acceptable 7 working day limit

explanation.text: The Logic: Mrs. Lakshmi's redemption was accepted on Monday at 2 PM (before the 3 PM cut-off), so Monday's NAV applied — this is the standard NAV-applicability rule. Under the SEBI redemption-payout regime, redemption/repurchase proceeds for an open-ended equity scheme must be transferred within the period specified by SEBI; the broadly cited industry turnaround is 3 working days (T+3), i.e., dispatch by Thursday. Since five working days have elapsed without receipt, the SEBI-specified period has been breached and the AMC owes delay interest at the SEBI-specified rate (commonly cited as 15% per annum). The correct course is: (1) lodge a written complaint with the AMC / investor service centre and demand the proceeds plus delay interest, (2) escalate to SEBI SCORES if not resolved within a reasonable time, and (3) use SEBI's Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) channel if still unresolved. The Trap: "Wait 10 working days" is incorrect — that exceeds the SEBI-specified turnaround for equity redemption. Redeeming further units to "test the system" is operationally and financially unwise and exposes her to further NAV risk. "Cannot complain — 7 working days is acceptable" misstates the timeline; the SEBI-specified period for equity redemption is shorter than 7 working days, and breach of the SEBI-specified period entitles the investor to delay interest. Note: The cited workbook (NISM Series V-A — Mutual Fund Distributors, pages 171, 192, 218-219) supports Monday-NAV applicability for a pre-cut-off redemption and states that redemption/repurchase proceeds are transferred "within the period specified by the Board" with interest "at the rate specified by SEBI," and that 15% p.a. applies expressly to delayed NFO refunds. The specific "3 working day" and "15% p.a. delay interest on redemption proceeds" claims used here are not stated in the cited pages and are framed above as the broader SEBI redemption-payout regime as commonly published.
